name: Amr ibn Murrah al-Jamali
nameAr: عمرو بن مرة بن عبد الله بن طارق الجملي المرادي، أبو عبد الله، الكوفي الأعمى

orthography.spelled: al-Jamali, with fathah on the jim and the mim

taqrib.ar: ثقة عابد، كان لا يدلس، ورمي بالإرجاء
taqrib.en: Reliable, devout; he did not practise tadlis; accused of holding irja'.

verdicts.en: Truthful, reliable; he held the view of irja'.

verdicts.ar: ما كان أفضل من عمرو بن مرة
verdicts.en: Asked who was the most virtuous person he had met: none was more virtuous than Amr ibn Murrah.

verdicts.source: Taqrib al-Tahdhib, entry 5112; Hady al-Sari, ch. 9, letter ayn

verdicts.ar: أحد الأثبات من صغار التابعين، متفق على توثيقه إلا أن بعضهم تكلم فيه لأنه كان يرى الإرجاء … وقد احتج به الجماعة
verdicts.en: One of the firm narrators among the younger Successors, agreed to be reliable, though some criticised him for holding irja'; all six relied on him.

dhahabi.ar: قال أبو حاتم: ثقة يرى الإرجاء
dhahabi.en: Abu Hatim: reliable; he held irja'.

flags.label: Irja' attributed to him
flags.detail: The Murji' view on faith and works was imputed to him; Ibn Hajar notes that this is the only reason some spoke against him and that his reliability is agreed upon. It does not affect this hadith, which concerns intention in fighting.

flags.label: Named only “Amr” in hadith 3126 and 2810
flags.detail: The full name Amr ibn Murrah appears in Muslim 1904a, Sunan Abi Dawud 2517 and Sunan al-Nasa'i 3136 on the same route from Shu'bah.

bio: A blind Kufan Successor of the fifth generation, counted among the firmest of his rank and remembered by his contemporaries for his piety. Shu'bah vouched that he did not use ambiguous formulas, so his “I heard Abu Wa'il” in hadith 3126 is characteristic. The one reservation about him, the accusation of irja', is doctrinal rather than a question of accuracy.

sources.label: Ibn Hajar, Hady al-Sari, ch. 9, letter ayn (Wikisource)
